maya: quick heads-up — ran a multi-region bench for a 13B-class model quantized to Q4x on A100 and H100 across us-east / us-west / eu-west. p50 mostly stable but p95 spikes in us-west when traffic is routed via the local edge-pop. dropping raw numbers + notes below, cc @alex

alex: can you paste the numbers and the plot link?

maya: sure — quick table from the synthetic run (batch mix, seq=1024, single-stream latency profile):

```
Model: redwood-13b-q4x
Config: batch mix (mostly 1), seq=1024, temp=0.0
GPU: A100 / H100
Region | Route    | GPU  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | qps
us-east | direct   | A100 | 58      | 120     | 180
us-east | edge-pop  | A100 | 62      | 140     | 170
us-west | direct   | A100 | 65      | 190     | 160
us-west | edge-pop  | A100 | 78      | 560     | 130  <-- large p95 jump
eu-west | direct   | H100 | 60      | 130     | 175
eu-west | edge-pop  | H100 | 64      | 150     | 165
us-west | direct   | H100 | 52      | 110     | 200
us-west | edge-pop  | H100 | 55      | 220     | 190
```

maya: TL;DR: A100 + edge-pop-usw sees a huge p95 tail. H100 is much less affected. throughput drops for the affected A100 edge route.

jun: quick runtime check — logs show kernel selection flips on the A100 edge nodes for certain leader sizes. we fall back from flash-attn-v2 to a cuBLAS-gemm slow path for some token shapes. that fallback + an extra serialization hop at the pop seems to produce the tail.

sam: can you repro with KV/prefix cache primed? if edge-pop is getting more cold traffic (more short-lived instances) that could explain the p95. also what was the client batching distribution?

maya: I ran a primed pass (warmed prefix cache with 10k priming requests) — p95 on A100 edge-pop drops from 560ms -> ~190ms, so priming helps but doesn't fully restore the direct baseline. primed run command we used: `wrk -t8 -c50 --latency --timeout 60s --script bench_prefix.lua http://edge-pop-usw/api/v1/generate`

jun: confirmed traces show a ~80ms extra serialization + ~200ms slow kernel execution on the slow requests. looks like the kernel selector heuristics choose a suboptimal kernel when combined with our edge packetization nuances. I can prototype a selection patch to prefer the stable kernel for small batch sizes on A100 in the pop.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: route-change executed — routed 15% of production traffic away from edge-pop-usw back to central-pop for a canary (route-canary-1842) at 2026-03-15T14:12Z :white_check_mark:

alex: good. next steps: 1) jun — adjust kernel selection threshold for A100 in edge-pop (urgent canary). 2) maya — add an optional "prefix-priming" flag to routing policy with TTL/size so we can opt-in for sensitive routes. 3) sam — run a capacity sweep for us-west (A100 pool) over the weekend and measure p50/p95 under primed vs cold. I'll sync Monday to review canary metrics. :+1:

sam: noted. I'll add the sweep to infra-runbook and schedule.

maya: attaching the plot link (internal): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/bench/multi-region-quant?panel=p50p95-usw-compare

alex: thanks — sharing with products + SRE after Monday canary results. we should also add a short note to the runbook about kernel fallbacks and how they interact with edge routing.

maya: agreed. I'll prepare a one-pager with the repro steps and the primary mitigation (kernel patch + prefix priming).

alex: perfect.
